clue.text: Go crazy in retirement

indicators.note: retiring is drawing back, so the word for crazy is read backwards

parts.note: bats is slang for mad or crazy

explanation.surface: Someone loses their mind once they have stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retirement' turns BATS round to give the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun synonym: to have a go at something is to have a try, an attempt.

clue.text: Nasty words written about new work, one to appear in the spring

definitions.text: one to appear in the spring

indicators.note: about means going round, so the rearranged letters surround the abbreviation for new
nasty letters are messed about, so the five of words are rearranged

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Unkind remarks written about a newly published piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nasty' rearranges WORDS to SOWDR; 'about' places N after its S. 'written' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small white flower blooming at the end of winter, among the first heralds of the new season.

clue.text: Consummate sailor terribly set on old instrument

indicators.note: in a down clue, set on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
so as an intensifier means very, terribly
a lute is an early plucked stringed instrument

explanation.surface: An expert sailor badly fixated on playing an antique instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective synonym: complete, perfect, total, as in a consummate professional.

clue.text: Fussy individual

definitions.meaning: hard to please, choosy about details
specific, relating to one single thing rather than others

explanation.definitionFit: Two adjective senses: exacting in standards, and distinct or specific to one case.

clue.text: Tree in a small enclosure

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a pen is a fenced enclosure for animals

explanation.surface: A sapling planted inside a little pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a poplar with trembling leaves.

clue.text: Insect flying right to me

indicators.note: flying letters are scattered in the air and land in a new order

explanation.surface: A bug buzzing straight at the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges RIGHT TO ME; the name is also that of a vintage biplane, apt for 'flying'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a moth with boldly striped or spotted wings.

clue.text: Remark about role in section

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the remark goes round the role

parts.note: a comment is a remark
a part is a role played by an actor

explanation.surface: A critic remarks on an actor's role in one segment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal, wrapping the remark round the role; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a separate division or space, as in a train carriage.

clue.text: Rope may appear after a trial gets rigged

indicators.note: a rigged trial is fixed or tampered with, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A noose may follow a fixed trial, the wild-west hanging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets rigged' rearranges A TRIAL. 'may appear after' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a lasso, a long rope with a running noose used by cowboys.

clue.text: Right price for taking up the Queen's jacket

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking up means lifting, so the word is read upwards

parts.note: a fee is a price charged
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: The proper cost of altering the Queen's jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking up' reverses FEE to EEF; 'for' and ''s' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a thick double-breasted jacket of the kind worn by sailors.

clue.text: Remove some raucous troublemakers

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An order to throw out a few of the noisy rowdies.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across raucOUS Troublemakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to expel or eject someone from a place or position.

clue.text: Meet guru, worried about the old man in dire straits

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the father
worried in the sense of fretted at, so these letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged
old man is informal for one's father, PA

explanation.surface: An anxious guru meeting someone's elderly father in a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges MEET GURU to UGUMTREE; 'about' puts PA after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: being stuck up a tree means being in serious difficulty with no easy way down.

clue.text: Creature at sea, old, injured flipper, we're told

indicators.note: injured letters are damaged and reshaped, so the three letters of old are rearranged
what we are told is heard, so the word for flipper is replaced by a spelling that sounds the same

parts.note: a fin is a flipper, the limb a sea creature swims with

explanation.surface: An aged sea animal has a hurt flipper, according to reports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' rearranges OLD to DOL; 'we're told' gives PHIN, spoken just like FIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a marine mammal of the whale family, found swimming in the oceans.

clue.text: On intimate terms in passing romance

parts.note: handing means passing over
love is romance

explanation.surface: A close friendship in a fleeting love affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: closely associated, working together in close collaboration.

clue.text: Beer club in Madrid backed by articles in two languages

indicators.note: backed by means followed by, so the articles come after the club

parts.note: Real Madrid is the famous Spanish football club
A is the English indefinite article and LE the French definite article

explanation.surface: A Spanish football club supported by newspaper pieces written in two languages.
explanation.walkthrough: Articles here are grammatical ones, not newspaper pieces: A in English, LE in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: traditional cask-conditioned British beer, as championed by the Campaign for Real Ale.

clue.text: Convalescent being thorough, taking in a book

indicators.note: taking in means holding inside, so the article and book go within the phrase

parts.note: out-and-out means complete or thorough, as in an out-and-out rogue

explanation.surface: A recovering patient is diligent about reading a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is only a link; 'taking in' is the container signal. 'Convalescent' is fair: a patient well enough to be up and around.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: someone up and moving around again after an illness is recovering, no longer confined to bed.

clue.text: Historical land in area is Roman, I suspect

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, so these letters are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: Someone guesses an ancient region lay in Roman territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I suspect' looks like the speaker's aside, but the I is fodder and 'suspect' rearranges IS ROMAN I.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the ancient name of Anatolia, the peninsula of modern Turkey.

clue.text: Heavenly in Dorset, here alone

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone finds bliss alone in the Dorset countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across dorsET HERE ALone. Dorset is an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: celestial, unearthly in delicacy.

clue.text: Staunch Conservative showing regret, depressed after time

indicators.note: after places the regret and depression following the time

parts.note: rue means regret
blue means sad or depressed

explanation.surface: A loyal Tory feels sorry and down after an election.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue is the colour of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a staunchly loyal supporter, especially of the Tories.

clue.text: Their sister trained a dog

indicators.note: trained letters are put through drills into a new order, so these eleven are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sibling of theirs has taught a dog its tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a red-coated gundog breed originating in Ireland.

clue.text: Perhaps Fonteyn cared desperately about Nureyev at first

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the initial
desperately suggests wild confusion, so the five letters are jumbled
at first takes the opening letter of the name

explanation.surface: Margot Fonteyn worried deeply about her partner Rudolf Nureyev.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desperately' rearranges CARED to DACER; 'about' sets N inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Margot Fonteyn was a celebrated prima ballerina.

clue.text: Stuff involving worker? Such may be classified

indicators.note: involving means containing, so the worker goes inside

parts.note: a wad is a lump of padding used to stuff something
an ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: Stuffing an employee in... a secret document?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Classified' suggests secrecy, but means classified ads in a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small newspaper advertisement asking for something.

clue.text: Marriage shown in publication Buddhist priest brought back

indicators.note: brought back means turned round, so the two words are read backwards together

parts.note: mag is short for magazine, a publication
a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk or priest

explanation.surface: A wedding reported in a magazine that a monk returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' reverses MAGLAMA as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative synonym: a union or blend of different things, a merger.

clue.text: Defiant words from heavy drinker in this place

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
here is the plain adverb for this spot

explanation.surface: A boozer shouting defiance at everyone in the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrase: a childish retort said to assert one has won or will not back down.

clue.text: Alarm shown by father and son? Not so

parts.note: sire means father

indicators.note: not says the following letters are removed from the word before

explanation.surface: Panic shown by a dad and boy? Perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not so' removes SO from SON, leaving N.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a warning device emitting a loud wailing sound.

clue.text: Economise in remote areas after failure

indicators.note: after places the remote areas following the failure

parts.note: a cut can be a failure, as in failing to make the cut
corners are out-of-the-way places, as in the far corners of the earth

explanation.surface: A business saving money in far-flung regions after a collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to skimp or take shortcuts in order to save money or effort.

clue.text: Fine spring

definitions.meaning: in good health, as in feeling fine
a natural source of water rising from the ground

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: healthy as an adjective, and a water source as a noun.

clue.text: Embarrassed-looking husband making mistake creates smokescreen

parts.note: red in the face, blushing
erring means going wrong or making an error

explanation.surface: A blushing husband whose blunder causes a cover-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative: a distraction meant to divert attention from the real issue.

clue.text: Joy needs shelter following onset of gale

indicators.note: following places the shelter after that letter
the onset is the beginning, so the first letter of gale is taken

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: Happiness depends on finding cover as a storm begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: delight or merriment.
